chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Abu Ja'far, from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man had intercourse with his wife while he was making up the days of Ramadan. He said: 'If he had intercourse with her before the Asr prayer, there is nothing upon him; he fasts one day in place of one day. And if he did so after Asr, he fasts that day and feeds ten poor people. And if he is unable to do so, he fasts three days as expiation for that.'

key_terms.يَوْمًا بَدَلَ يَوْمٍ: One day in place of one day

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a man who has intercourse with his wife while making up missed Ramadan fasts?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific expiation (kaffarah) for a man who engages in sexual intercourse with his wife while making up missed Ramadan fasts, distinguishing rulings based on whether it occurs before or after the Asr prayer. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the penalty scales with the timing of the act, requiring either a single make-up day, or a combination of feeding ten poor people and fasting three days if the act occurs later in the day. This ruling underscores the importance of maintaining the sanctity of the fasting period even during make-up obligations.
